### `CYLBadgeView/CYLBadgeAppearance.h`

| iOS 公开 API / iOS public API | 鸿蒙对应实现 / HarmonyOS implementation | 接口注释 / Comment |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `CYLBadgeAppearance` | `CYLBadgeAppearance` (built; emulator check pending / 已编译，模拟器验证待做) | App-wide default badge style. Most apps use the same badge everywhere (a red background, white text, one font, the same corner offset), but each badge property belongs to one object, so it had to be set on every tab, bar button and view again. Set the defaults here once, typically in `-application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:`, before showing badges: CYLBadgeAppearance *appearance = [CYLBadgeAppearance globalAppearance]; appearance.backgroundColor = [UIColor systemPinkColor]; appearance.font = [UIFont boldSystemFontOfSize:10]; appearance.centerOffset = CGPointMake(-2, 2); Precedence: a value set on an object (e.g. `viewController.cyl_badgeBackgroundColor`) wins over the global one; the global one wins over the built-in default. This covers every badge host: UIViewController, UITabBarItem, UIBarButtonItem, UIControl and UIView. Badges created later use the new defaults. A badge already on screen picks up new colors, font and border the next time it is shown (`-cyl_showBadgeValue:animationType:`); a red dot keeps its size and position until its style changes. So set the appearance before showing badges. Use it on the main thread, like the rest of UIKit. |
| `CYLBadgeAppearance globalAppearance` | `CYLBadgeAppearance.globalAppearance` (built; emulator check pending / 已编译，模拟器验证待做) | The shared global appearance. In Swift: `CYLBadgeAppearance.global`. |

| `CYLFlatDesignTabBar 0` | TODO: N/A on HarmonyOS: FlatDesign is the iOS-only KVC tab bar; the HarmonyOS tab bar is one ArkUI component | The `UITabBarAppearance` of the flat design tab bar, like `-[UITabBar standardAppearance]`: one appearance object styles the system tab bar (Liquid Glass and the classic style) and this tab bar alike. Nil (the default) keeps the flat design look and the properties below. `CYLTabBarController` assigns `tabBarController.tabBar.standardAppearance` here when the app has set one, so setting the system tab bar's appearance is enough; assigning this property directly also works. When the selected item has its own `-[CYLFlatDesignTabBarItem standardAppearance]`, the whole bar uses that one while it is selected, as `UITabBar` does. Mapping (UITabBarAppearance → flat design tab bar): backgroundEffect → the background blur (nil: no blur) backgroundColor → the background color backgroundImage → the background image backgroundImageContentMode → the background image's content mode shadowImage → the top shadow line (its own height; tinted by shadowColor if template) shadowColor → a hairline at the top when there is no shadowImage (nil/clear: none) selectionIndicatorImage → drawn behind the selected item selectionIndicatorTintColor → tints the selection indicator image stackedItemPositioning → .centered lays the items out centered; .fill / .automatic fill the width stackedItemWidth → the item width when centered (0: equal share of the width) stackedItemSpacing → the spacing between items when centered stackedLayoutAppearance.normal / .selected / .disabled (UITabBarItemStateAppearance): titleTextAttributes → title font, color and other attributes (they override the item's own) titlePositionAdjustment → the title offset when the item has none (`CYLTabBarController.titlePositionAdjustment` wins, as on the system tab bar) iconColor → the icon tint color (template images) badgeBackgroundColor → the badge background color badgeTextAttributes → the badge font and text color badgePositionAdjustment → the badge center offset Not mapped: inline/compact inline layouts (the flat design bar is always stacked), scroll edge appearances, `badgeTitlePositionAdjustment` and the focused state. Badge values a state does not customize (equal to a new `UITabBarAppearance`) leave the badge's own settings and `CYLBadgeAppearance` in place. |

| `CYLFlatDesignTabBar useLayoutSafeAreaInsets` | TODO | Whether the buttons stay clear of the left/right safe area (e.g. a landscape notch). The background always spans the full width. The one-sided inset of a vertical status bar (the folded iPhone Duo's right-hand status column) is controlled separately by `respectsVerticalStatusBarSafeArea` (ignored by default). |
| `CYLFlatDesignTabBar respectsVerticalStatusBarSafeArea` | TODO: N/A on HarmonyOS: HarmonyOS has no vertical status bar column beside the app (the iOS 84 pt side column); the status bar is always at the top. | Default is NO. Whether the buttons also stay clear of the inset that a vertical status bar adds on one side, e.g. the 84 pt column on the right of the folded iPhone Duo held upright (iOS 27.1 SDK), where the status bar (Wi-Fi, battery) moves to the trailing edge. NO: that one-sided inset is ignored, so the buttons span the full width and stay centered on screen; the last button can sit partly under the status column. YES: the buttons stay inside the safe area, so the row is shifted left by that column. A vertical status bar is told apart by its inset being on one side only; a landscape notch insets both sides and is still handled by `useLayoutSafeAreaInsets`. Has no effect when `useLayoutSafeAreaInsets` is NO. Only matters while the vertical bar is shown. This property does not switch the vertical bar on or off; that is `CYLTabBarController.allowsVerticalBar` (or a screen's own `preferredVerticalBarBehavior`). With the vertical bar off the status bar is horizontal, there is no one-sided inset, and both values give the same layout. |

| `CYLTabBar tabImageViewDefaultOffset` | TODO | The default offset needed to vertically center the `TabImageView`. @attention This value is used for both top and bottom; the operation is equivalent to the following: `viewController.tabBarItem.imageInsets = UIEdgeInsetsMake(tabImageViewDefaultOffset, 0, -tabImageViewDefaultOffset, 0);` |
| `CYLTabBar syncsClassicStylesToAppearance` | TODO | Since iOS 13 UIKit ignores the classic styles (`tintColor`, `barTintColor`, `unselectedItemTintColor`, `backgroundImage`, `shadowImage`, `barStyle`) once the tab bar uses `UITabBarAppearance`. When YES (default), each classic setter also writes its value into `standardAppearance` (and `scrollEdgeAppearance` when there is one), so both ways of styling work together; only a value that changed is written. Not with Liquid Glass, where the system draws the bar. Set NO to keep UIKit's own behavior. |
| `CYLTabBar context` | TODO | This can be left unset; the default is CYLTabBarController. If set, please implement the `+[CYLPlusButton tabBarContext]` method in CYLPlusButton and ensure consistency. If neither is implemented, the default is CYLTabBarController for both. |

Default `UIEdgeInsetsZero` (the layout is exactly as before). Works with and without a plus button, and together with centered positioning (docs/Tab-Item-Positioning.md). Liquid Glass and FlatDesign are not affected. ((CYLTabBar *)tabBarController.tabBar).cyl_itemEdgeInsets = UIEdgeInsetsMake(0, 16, 0, 16); |

### `CYLTabBarConfigurationParser.h`

| iOS 公开 API / iOS public API | 鸿蒙对应实现 / HarmonyOS implementation | 接口注释 / Comment |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `CYLTabBarConfigurationFormat` | `CYLTabBarConfigurationFormat` (built; emulator check pending / 已编译，模拟器验证待做) | The key-value file formats a tab bar configuration can be written in (see `-[CYLTabBarController initWithConfiguration:]`). Every format gives the same dictionary: its keys are the configuration and item keys (`CYLTabBarControllerContext`, `CYLTabBarItemTitle`, ...). |
| `CYLTabBarConfigurationErrorDomain` | `CYLTabBarConfigurationErrorDomain` (built; emulator check pending / 已编译，模拟器验证待做) | Error domain of the configuration parser and loaders. |
| `CYLTabBarConfigurationErrorCode` | `CYLTabBarConfigurationErrorCode` (built; emulator check pending / 已编译，模拟器验证待做) | — |
| `CYLTabBarConfigurationMaximumLength` | `CYLTabBarConfigurationMaximumLength` (built; emulator check pending / 已编译，模拟器验证待做) | The largest file or response read: 5 MB. |
| `CYLTabBarConfigurationMaximumDepth` | `CYLTabBarConfigurationMaximumDepth` (built; emulator check pending / 已编译，模拟器验证待做) | The deepest nesting accepted: 64 levels, far more than a configuration needs, far less than overflows the stack. |
| `CYLTabBarConfigurationParser` | `CYLTabBarConfigurationParser` (built; emulator check pending / 已编译，模拟器验证待做) | Reads key-value configuration files into dictionaries, in every `CYLTabBarConfigurationFormat`. Foundation only, no UIKit: the values stay strings, numbers, booleans, arrays and dictionaries; `CYLTabBarController` turns them into insets, offsets, sizes, URLs and images (see `-[CYLTabBarController initWithConfiguration:]`). Binary Protocol Buffers use the built-in schema of Configurations/cyl_tabbar_configuration.proto. Text formats are read as UTF-8. YAML, TOML, INI, .properties and XML give unquoted `true` / `false` as booleans and numbers as NSNumber; YAML and TOML support the common subset used for configuration (no anchors, tags or multi-line block scalars in YAML; no dates in TOML). |

| `CYLTabBarController titlePositionAdjustment` | `CYLTabBarController.titlePositionAdjustment` (@Prop) (built; emulator check pending / 已编译，模拟器验证待做) | The title offset of every tab. A tab's own `CYLTabBarItemTitlePositionAdjustment` takes precedence over it. Settable at runtime: setting it re-applies the offset to the tabs already added and lays them out again. On iOS 13+ UIKit ignores `-[UITabBarItem titlePositionAdjustment]` once the tab bar uses `UITabBarAppearance` (e.g. after `tabBar.standardAppearance = ...`), so the offset is also written into a copy of the tab bar's `standardAppearance` (and `scrollEdgeAppearance` on iOS 15+) installed on each tab with an offset. Changes the app makes to the tab bar's appearance later are picked up on the next layout. `UIOffsetZero` leaves the tabs untouched, so an offset set through the appearance proxy or `UITabBarAppearance` still applies (issue #583). Works for all tab bar styles: the classic system tab bar, Liquid Glass (iOS 26+) and FlatDesign. |
| `CYLTabBarController automaticallyAdjustsImageOnlyTabs` | TODO | Whether image-only tabs (tabs without a title) are adjusted automatically. Default is YES. When the first tab button has no title label, the classic tab bar measures once how far the image has to move to be vertically centered (`-[CYLTabBar tabImageViewDefaultOffset]`), then, for every tab whose item has no title, sets `imageInsets` to that offset and moves the empty title out of the way (`titlePositionAdjustment`). A value of the app is never replaced: tabs with a title, an item with its own `imageInsets` or `titlePositionAdjustment` (set on the item or with `CYLTabBarItemImageInsets` / `CYLTabBarItemTitlePositionAdjustment`), and a non-zero controller-level `imageInsets` / `titlePositionAdjustment` are left as they are. Set it to NO to turn the adjustment off and lay out the tabs yourself: the tab bar stops measuring, and the values it had already written are restored. Set it before the tab bar is laid out (in `-init…` or `-viewDidLoad`) to avoid seeing the icons move once. Classic tab bar only (including Liquid Glass); FlatDesign never adjusts tabs. |

| `CYLTabBarController allowsVerticalBar` | TODO: N/A on HarmonyOS: the iPhone Duo vertical bar of iOS 27.1 | Whether the system may show the bars in the vertical bar: a column on the leading or trailing edge that iOS 27.1 uses on some devices, such as the folded iPhone Duo. Defaults to NO. - NO: CYLTabBarController returns `UIVerticalBarBehaviorDisabled` from `preferredVerticalBarBehavior`, so the tab bar stays at the bottom and the status bar stays horizontal. Exception (issue #672): a screen that overrides `preferredVerticalBarBehavior` itself (the selected view controller, or the top view controller of a selected navigation controller) still decides for itself, e.g. return `UIVerticalBarBehaviorAutomatic` to opt in. - YES: the system default behaviour, as in 1.99.65 and earlier. `UITabBarController` passes the choice to the selected view controller, so each screen can still opt out by overriding `preferredVerticalBarBehavior`. This is a convenience switch for UIKit's `preferredVerticalBarBehavior`; a subclass may override that property directly instead. Changes apply immediately: the setter calls `setNeedsUpdateOfVerticalBarConfiguration`. Not related to `tabBarController.sidebar.preferredPlacement` / `sidebar.isAvailable` (iOS 27): those choose between the tab bar and an iPad-style sidebar when there is room for one (regular width) and need the `UITab` API; the vertical bar is used in compact width, where the sidebar is not available. Status with YES: Liquid Glass style verified on the iPhone Duo simulator (layout, Lottie icons, badges, plus button, re-tap, long press and drag). FlatDesign style verified on the iPhone Duo simulator: the status bar moves to the trailing column and the FlatDesign bar stays at the bottom with its items centered across the full width (see `CYLFlatDesignTabBar.respectsVerticalStatusBarSafeArea`). Folded iPhone Duo, FlatDesign, vertical status bar with centered items: tabBarController.allowsVerticalBar = YES; // respectsVerticalStatusBarSafeArea keeps its default NO No effect below iOS 27.1 or when built with an SDK older than iOS 27.1. |

| `CYLTabBarController(CYLTabBarMinimize) cyl_tabBarMinimizeBehavior` | `CYLTabBarController.tabBarMinimizeBehavior` (@Prop) + `cyl_reportScroll(delta)` (built; emulator check pending / 已编译，模拟器验证待做) | How the tab bar reacts when the current page scrolls. Default `CYLTabBarMinimizeBehaviorAutomatic`. - Liquid Glass on iOS 26+ (every style except FlatDesign): sets the native `UITabBarController.tabBarMinimizeBehavior`. The system shrinks the tab bar and picks the scroll view; choose it with `-[UIViewController setContentScrollView:forEdge:]` when a page has several. - FlatDesign: hides the tab bar with `-setTabBarHidden:animated:` when the selected page (the top page of a navigation controller) scrolls, and shows it again on the opposite scroll, when the page scrolls back to the top (OnScrollDown), and when another tab or page appears. A tab bar hidden by your own `-setTabBarHidden:` is left hidden. The scroll view is the page's `-contentScrollViewForEdge:NSDirectionalRectEdgeBottom`, otherwise the first scroll view in its view hierarchy. - Classic tab bar (every style except FlatDesign on iOS 25 and earlier, and on iOS 26 in UI compatibility mode): the system tab bar, with its plus button, is hidden with `-setTabBarHidden:animated:` when the selected page scrolls, and shown on the opposite scroll, at the top (OnScrollDown) and when another tab or page appears (animated by UIKit on iOS 18 and later, as FlatDesign before iOS 18). Pages pushed with `hidesBottomBarWhenPushed` are left to UIKit, and a tab bar at the top (not at the bottom) is never hidden. FlatDesign and the classic tab bar hide through the same public `-setTabBarHidden:animated:` you can call yourself; a tab bar you hid with it stays hidden. Can be set at any time, before or after the view loads. When it comes back (issue #13, as in the Facebook app): the bar hides only while the user drags down through content; it comes back at once, in every style, on background / foreground switches, a call, any system or in-app alert, a modal page, another key window, a push notification, a push or pop, and a memory warning, and hides again only on a new drag. Robust by design: a whitelist, not a list of events. The bar stays hidden only inside a hide session, started by the user scrolling down and bound to its context (page, tab, scroll view, window); anything else, also this controller's appear / disappear / size change and the keyboard, ends it and shows the bar. See docs/TabBar-Minimize-On-Scroll.md, "When the tab bar hides, and when it comes back". Same switch, Apple's API: on iOS 26+, `tabBarController.tabBarMinimizeBehavior = UITabBarMinimizeBehaviorOnScrollDown` does exactly the same in every style (CYLTabBarController overrides it; both read and write one value). Use this property where iOS 25 and earlier must be supported, since Apple's property does not exist there. |
| `CYLTabBarController(CYLTabBarMinimize) cyl_hidesTabBarOnScroll` | `CYLTabBarController.hidesTabBarOnScroll` (@Prop) (built; emulator check pending / 已编译，模拟器验证待做) | The most direct switch: hide the tab bar while the page scrolls down, show it again when it scrolls back up. Named like UIKit's `hidesBarsOnSwipe` and `hidesBottomBarWhenPushed`, and the same feature as `cyl_tabBarMinimizeBehavior`, which it reads and writes: tabBarController.cyl_hidesTabBarOnScroll = YES; // == cyl_tabBarMinimizeBehavior = OnScrollDown tabBarController.cyl_hidesTabBarOnScroll = NO; // == cyl_tabBarMinimizeBehavior = Never What YES does in each style: - Liquid Glass (iOS 26+): calls Apple's own `UITabBarController.tabBarMinimizeBehavior = OnScrollDown`; the system minimizes the tab bar. - FlatDesign: the flat tab bar is hidden and shown with `-setTabBarHidden:animated:` while the page scrolls. - Classic tab bar (iOS 25 and earlier, e.g. iOS 17, and iOS 26 in UI compatibility mode): the system tab bar is hidden and shown with `-setTabBarHidden:animated:`, with FlatDesign's animation before iOS 18. The getter is YES while scroll hiding is on in either direction (OnScrollDown or OnScrollUp). Use `cyl_tabBarMinimizeBehavior` for OnScrollUp or Automatic. |

### `CYLUtils/CYLResourceRoute.h`

| iOS 公开 API / iOS public API | 鸿蒙对应实现 / HarmonyOS implementation | 接口注释 / Comment |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `CYLResourceRoute` | TODO | Resource routes: one string that says where a resource is (a configuration file, a folder of string tables…), built into the app or in its sandbox (e.g. downloaded at run time), the same on iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter (docs/Resource-Routes.md). The prefix decides, in this order: bundle:<path> the app's resources (Android: assets) sandbox:Documents/<path> Documents (Android: filesDir) sandbox:Caches/<path> Library/Caches (Android: cacheDir); sandbox:tmp/<path> the temporary folder sandbox:<path> below the app's home folder (Android: the app's data folder) file:///<path> a local file URL /<path> an absolute path ~/<path> the app's home folder <path> relative to `baseDirectory` (a configuration file's folder), else the app's resources A query picks one file in that folder: `name`, and optionally `theme`, `version` and `format`, for files named `{name}[-{theme}][@{version}].{format}`. Without `version` the highest one wins; without `format` any format the configuration parser reads, preferring JSON, YAML, plist, XML, TOML, then the others: sandbox:Caches/tabbar?name=tabbar&theme=dark&version=2.1&format=json → …/Caches/tabbar/tabbar-dark@2.1.json bundle:Configurations?name=tabbar → the highest tabbar[@version].{json,…} The library never ships these resources: string tables and configuration files belong to the app. |
| `CYLResourceRoute +pathForRoute:baseDirectory:` | TODO | — |
| `CYLResourceRoute +pathOfFileInDirectory:name:theme:version:format:` | TODO | — |

(`-cyl_languageCellForTableView:`), row 1 the memory warning check (`-cyl_memoryWarningCellForTableView:`), row 2 switches the title offset of all tabs (`CYLTabBarController.titlePositionAdjustment`, #19), row 5 shows the plus button's touchable area and scales it with a slider (issue #91), row 6 selects the next tab by its index without the plus button (`cyl_selectedIndexIgnoringPlusButton`, issue #515), row 7 switches how the tab bar minimizes or hides on scroll (`cyl_tabBarMinimizeBehavior`, issue #13), row 8 switches the tap animation of the tabs, row 9 turns on the long press of the tabs, row 10 turns on swiping to switch tabs, row 11 shows a subview that responds outside its superview, row 12 loads an image from a bundle, row 13 hides the navigation bar without a base class, row 14 opens the slide transition demo, row 15 switches the tap sound and haptic, row 16 switches the long press duration and double tap interval, row 17 switches to the previous or next tab, row 18 runs the CYLUtils weak associated object and nearest control helpers (issue #535), row 19 pushes a tab bar controller whose plus button gets its image later (loaded, replaced, removed, or a background image), row 20 picks a skin (theme) of the tab bar (`CYLThemeManager`, `CYLTabBarTheme`, issue #216), row 21 lists the scroll hiding simulations in an action sheet (`-cyl_presentScrollHideSimulationMenu`, issue #13), row 22 creates a tab bar controller from a configuration file or URL (`UIViewController+CYLConfigurationDemo.h`), then the simulated failures of configurations, one row each (`-cyl_configurationEdgeCaseCellForTableView:row:`), then the in-place tab item updates (`-cyl_tabBarItemUpdateCellForTableView:row:`): title, icon, network icon, all network icons, all local icons, GIF icon, all titles, replace neighboring tabs. |
